title: Senior Architect: Evaluate a Late Brief Change
prompt: You are a senior architect advising fictional Alder Library on a late concept change. Supplied change memo: "Move the quiet study room beside the loading area to create a larger event space. Cost neutral; issue the revised client set tomorrow." Current brief requires quiet study during daytime deliveries. Cost sheet covers partition materials only; it excludes acoustic assessment, consultant coordination, and document revision time. No revised adjacency review or client decision is recorded. Exercise policy requires a change decision to state scope, affected requirements, evidence gaps, responsible reviewers, and client acceptance before the set is described as approved. Review the memo and propose a proportionate decision route. No construction advice or legal contract interpretation is required.
blurb: Challenge an incomplete cost-neutral claim and structure a client decision around a changed requirement.

rubric.label: Trace the change to the brief
rubric.description: Identifies the conflict beyond the immediate space gain.

anchors.0: Accepts the move because the event space becomes larger.
anchors.2: Identifies quiet-study conflict with daytime loading.
anchors.4: Explains that adjacency changes threaten an explicit concurrent-use requirement, identifies affected acoustic/access coordination questions, and distinguishes unresolved checks from proven defects.

rubric.label: Challenge the scope of the estimate
rubric.description: Avoids treating a partial material comparison as total impact.

anchors.0: Repeats cost neutral or invents a precise full cost.
anchors.2: Notes that the sheet excludes assessment, coordination, and revision time.
anchors.4: Separates known material cost from unpriced design/consultant/schedule impacts, requests bounded estimates, and presents uncertainty without claiming the change is necessarily unaffordable.

rubric.label: Provide proportionate options and authorization
rubric.description: Keeps an unapproved variant from appearing accepted.

anchors.0: Issues the revision as approved without client agreement.
anchors.2: Requests review and client decision before approval.
anchors.4: Offers a time-bounded option comparison, assigns specialist checks and a client decision owner, permits a clearly labeled study variant if useful, and defines the evidence needed to update the issue status and brief.

reference.scenario: You are a senior architect advising fictional Alder Library on a late concept change. Supplied change memo: "Move the quiet study room beside the loading area to create a larger event space. Cost neutral; issue the revised client set tomorrow." Current brief requires quiet study during daytime deliveries. Cost sheet covers partition materials only; it excludes acoustic assessment, consultant coordination, and document revision time. No revised adjacency review or client decision is recorded. Exercise policy requires a change decision to state scope, affected requirements, evidence gaps, responsible reviewers, and client acceptance before the set is described as approved. Review the memo and propose a proportionate decision route. No construction advice or legal contract interpretation is required.

facts.value: The client can review alternatives in two working days. The acoustics consultant can perform an initial desk review tomorrow but cannot certify performance from the current sketch.
An alternative keeps the quiet room in place and gains a smaller event-space increase by relocating nonpublic storage; storage access effects have not been assessed.
The delivery schedule is controlled by a separate operator; no agreement to change it exists.
facts.reveal_when: candidate suggests moving deliveries to solve the conflict

model_points: The change trades an explicit quiet-use requirement for a larger event space. It may be feasible with a revised brief or supporting design, but the memo has not shown that.
A partition-only comparison does not justify a total cost-neutral statement. Request the missing estimates and specialist questions without manufacturing numerical precision.
Provide the client a decision with consequences and clear status. A labeled study issue can support discussion; an approved issue requires the stated review and acceptance under the exercise policy.

probes.trigger: candidate asks for more cost information but omits the quiet-use conflict
probes.question: Which existing client requirement changes even if material cost is unchanged?

probes.trigger: candidate proposes changing the delivery schedule
probes.question: Whose agreement would make that a credible option, and what remains unresolved until then?

probes.trigger: candidate initially agrees to issue tomorrow then revises
probes.question: How would you correct the issue status and explain the revised decision timetable?

fair_alternatives: Retain the current brief, investigate the proposed move, or compare the storage alternative; any can be recommended with explicit assumptions and ownership.
A clearly labeled unapproved study set can be shared for discussion if it is not confused with the client-approved design.

Assess the work demonstrated here. Accept relevant examples from education, volunteering, caregiving, placements, or paid work; professional vocabulary and employer pedigree are not evidence of a stronger answer.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess senior architectural coordination and client decision quality. Do not certify acoustics, building-code compliance, construction safety, or contractual entitlements. Unobserved dimensions are not failures. Credit a reasoned correction and distinguish independently demonstrated reasoning from coached assistance. Do not penalize a candidate for an unrevealed conditional fact; credit appropriate requests and conditional plans, and distinguish candidate assumptions from interviewer-supplied evidence.

interviewer_notes: Assess senior architectural coordination and client decision quality. Do not certify acoustics, building-code compliance, construction safety, or contractual entitlements. Use only the supplied fictional facts and policies; acknowledge unknowns. Ask one triggered probe at a time after the candidate has finished. Accept plain language and accessible written or spoken explanations. Do not score accent, typing speed, confidence, credentials, or experience with a named employer. Credit revisions and record assistance. All participants are fictional adults; no real patient, client, operational, or confidential data is needed. Allow silence for thinking without treating it as failure. In short sessions prioritize the core decision and one material follow-up, leaving room for a correction and wrap-up.

learning_drills.title: Write a decision-ready change note
learning_drills.prompt: Write a six-line change note covering benefit, threatened requirement, partial cost, alternatives, reviewers, and client decision. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
checklist: Link the change to the quiet-use requirement
Separate partial estimate from total cost
